chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A bull at al-Kufa went on a rampage, so the people rushed toward it with their swords and struck it down. Then they came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked him, and he said: It was a valid slaughter while alive, and its flesh is permissible.

key_terms.حَلَال: Halal — permissible; the legal ruling that the meat is lawful to consume
key_terms.ذَكَاة: Dhaka — the Islamic act of ritual slaughter; here referring to a valid slaughter under emergency circumstances
key_terms.وَحِيَّة: Wahiyya — alive/vital; indicating the animal was still alive when struck, making the killing a valid slaughter

ai.seo_question: Is an animal that escaped and was killed with a sword in Islam considered halal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a ruling attributed to Imam Ali (AS) concerning a bull that escaped and was killed by people in al-Kufa without a formal slaughter. Imam Ali (AS) ruled that since the animal was slaughtered while still alive (not yet dead from injury), the killing counted as a valid slaughter (dhaka) and the meat was lawful. This reflects the jurisprudential principle that an animal in imminent danger may be killed in any manner that hastens death while it is still alive.
